clue.text: Insubstantial character on committee

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person, a character
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: Someone on a committee is dismissed as a lightweight with no real presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing one piece after the other in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy and unconvincing, like a stock fictional figure, is called pasteboard-thin or insubstantial.

clue.text: Stores film, preserving one group of stars

indicators.note: preserving here means keeping something held inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: film is stored in cans, the reels' tins
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A warehouse keeps hold of a movie reel and protects it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserving' puts I inside CANS. Canis Major and Canis Minor are the constellations of the big and little dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis is the Latin dog name used for two constellations, each a named grouping of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Put in new order for back number

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a number or assortment of things, as in a range of goods

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a back issue of a magazine to be ordered again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'back number' looks like an old issue but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift items into a fresh sequence is to reorganise them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Railing with bluster, a DA, fuming

indicators.note: fuming suggests a wild, agitated state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A district attorney rails angrily in a blustering rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuming' rearranges BLUSTER, A and DA together. 'Railing' looks like ranting, to match the surface, but means a fence of banisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a row of small pillars topped by a rail, a kind of railing on stairs or balconies.

clue.text: Material for a lyric maybe with lead for cello

indicators.note: maybe hints that the words could be arranged in some other way, signalling a rearrangement
the lead of a word is its opening letter, taken from the word cello

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about fabric for a song lyric written for a cellist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges A LYRIC into ACRYLI, and 'lead for cello' adds C. The surface reads 'with lead for cello' as a song being scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre and fabric, a kind of material for clothes.

clue.text: Diminished by degrees in performance

indicators.note: in places the degrees inside the word for performance

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: Something gradually lessened during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by degrees' looks like 'gradually', but 'by' is only a link and the degrees are Bachelor of Arts ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to lower in quality or value, so a debased thing has been reduced.

clue.text: Dance, look, during intermission

indicators.note: during means within a span of time, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a gap is a break or intermission
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Someone checks out a dance during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' reads as a verb in the surface, but gives the old exclamation lo.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a lively 19th-century ballroom dance in quick duple time.

clue.text: Rip off most of gutter

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gully is a gutter or channel for water

explanation.surface: Someone tears away most of the guttering from a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of GULLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to cheat or dupe them, which is to swindle or rip them off.

clue.text: River of Italy, in mythology

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for mythology

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or myth
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A river that features in Italian legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. The Loire is in France, so the Italian setting misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest waterway in France, flowing to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Jail? Figure in cooler shows remorse

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, and slang for a prison

indicators.note: in places the number inside the word for cooler

parts.note: ice is a cooler for drinks
ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A prisoner's number on a cell door in a prison shows contrition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is also slang for jail, tempting a second prison piece; here it is ICE. 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is sorrow for wrongdoing, the same feeling as regret or contrition.

clue.text: A name in Ulster? Quite

parts.note: Ulster is commonly used for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
all means completely, quite

explanation.surface: A query whether some name is a fully Northern Irish one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. Niall is a traditional Irish first name, so the definition is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Niall is an Irish male forename, so it is one example of a personal name.

clue.text: Cloudy beer left by celebrity in revolt

indicators.note: cloudy beer is murky and stirred up, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: Customers rise up when a star leaves them with hazy beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloudy' rearranges BEER into REBE. 'by' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion is an uprising against authority, the same as an insurrection.

clue.text: Start of speech, bald, seemingly, with no evidence of accent

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from speech

parts.note: bald people appear to have no tresses, no locks of hair

explanation.surface: A bald speaker opens a talk with no sign of a regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' means stress on a syllable, not a regional way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking stress means unaccented, carrying no emphasis on any syllable.

clue.text: Discharge old soldier without name

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a vet is short for veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran is let go from the army without being named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here, so VET goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To vent is to let out or release, as steam or anger is released.

clue.text: Torch made from timber left in exit

indicators.note: in places the timber and the left inside the word for exit

parts.note: flight is escape, an exit
ash is a timber

explanation.surface: A torch is improvised from wood left at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashlight is the American name for a hand-held electric torch.

clue.text: Of a class in Greece, endlessly warring

indicators.note: warring suggests conflict and disorder, so the letters are scrambled
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Something typical of a social class in Greece, which is always at war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts GREECE to GREEC, and 'warring' rearranges IN and GREEC together.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means relating to a whole group or kind rather than a single member.

clue.text: Understanding displayed by amateur in grand operatic work

indicators.note: in places the amateur inside the grand opera pieces

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

explanation.surface: Insight shown by a novice performing in a grand opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' is a link. 'Gathering that...' can replace 'Understanding that...'. Wagner's 'The Ring' is a four-opera cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to infer, so gathering, like comprehending, means grasping something from what is said.

clue.text: Swimmer left in river, nursing injured hip

indicators.note: in places the left inside the river
nursing means holding close, so the river holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: the Don is a river in England, Scotland and Russia

indicators.note: injured means damaged or bent out of shape, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A swimmer with an injured hip is helped along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' turns the hip into PHI; 'in' and 'nursing' both say the river holds the left and that. The Don is a river in Yorkshire, Scotland and Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal, a strong swimmer.

clue.text: Spouse with pocket sewing kit

explanation.surface: A married woman carries a little needle-and-thread pouch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link between the two definitions. The sewing-kit sense is old, also spelt hussif.
explanation.definitionFit: A married woman running a home is a partner in marriage; the same word names a small case of needles and thread.

clue.text: Machine lever rated faulty by the Parisian

indicators.note: faulty suggests something broken or wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Parisian judges a lever on a machine to be defective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges RATED to TREAD; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that drives a machine such as a sewing machine or loom.

clue.text: Raises fees idiots reduced by 50%, stupidly

indicators.note: stupidly suggests muddled thinking, so the letters are jumbled
halving the six-letter word leaves its first three letters

explanation.surface: Fees are foolishly halved for fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by 50%' keeps IDI of IDIOTS, and 'stupidly' rearranges it with FEES.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to improve someone morally or intellectually, lifting them up.

clue.text: It's enough to make you livery

definitions.text: It's enough to make you livery

parts.words: It's enough to make you livery
parts.note: 'livery' reads as feeling bilious, but a livery is a servant's uniform, and an outfit puts you in one

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's enough to make you sick' is the phrase being bent: livery here is an adjective formed from the uniform called livery.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes, and livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants.

clue.text: Stacey sported eastern gemstone

indicators.note: a sport is a mutation, so a sported word has changed its form

explanation.surface: Stacey wore an oriental gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sported' looks like 'wore' but rearranges STACEY into CATSEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-eye is a gem such as chrysoberyl showing a band of light like a cat's pupil.

clue.text: Diocese containing miles of woodland

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the diocese wraps the miles

parts.note: Ely is a diocese and cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A diocese covers many miles of forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmy describes a place full of elms, the trees that make up such woodland.

clue.text: Gold, former money, turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman
M is the abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3

explanation.surface: Some gold, and old currency, has been found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses LATE plus M; 'turned up' looks like 'found'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is one example of a metal.

clue.text: Source of drink I'd knocked back (smooth blend of rye)

indicators.note: knocked back means drunk down, and here the letters are reversed

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
still water is smooth and calm

indicators.note: a blend of things mixes them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a smooth whisky blended from rye at the source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns ID into DI, and 'blend of' rearranges RYE into ERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery produces spirits such as whisky, so it is where those drinks come from.

clue.text: Submit financial returns

explanation.surface: Someone hands in their figures on investment income.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way is to surrender; the same word means the income an investment returns.

clue.text: Problem for north in slump

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for slump

parts.note: a sag is a slump or droop

explanation.surface: A difficulty for the North of the country during a recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected obstacle or drawback.

clue.text: In future maybe four will be roped in (detailed)

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: roped in means captured and held inside, so the tense surrounds the number

parts.note: the future is one tense of a verb
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: In future, four people will be enlisted to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive means thorough and concentrated, giving close attention to detail.

clue.text: In speech ridicules pretence

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word is heard

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or ridicule them

explanation.surface: Someone who mocks pretension in their talk.
explanation.walkthrough: To guy is to make fun of, from Guy Fawkes effigies.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance put on to conceal the truth, a show or front.

clue.text: Silence around mid-July in camp

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the silence wraps the middle letters

parts.note: to gag is to silence

indicators.note: mid takes the middle letters of the word July

explanation.surface: Quiet descends in the middle of July at a summer camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' gives UL, the middle of JULY. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour prison camps.

clue.text: Knot these loose boots initially with waxed thread

indicators.note: loose means not held in place, so the letters move freely
initially takes the first letter of the word boots

parts.note: a waxed end is a cobbler's thread, the end

explanation.surface: Someone ties boots loosely using cobbler's waxed thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges THESE into SHEET. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet bend is a sailor's hitch for joining two ropes.
